title: Counting C. elegans Nematodes
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5ung6ve

steps.title: Homogenize worm solution
steps.instruction: Shake the wormy solution thoroughly to make the concentration of worms more homogeneous.

steps.title: Prepare streak slide
steps.instruction: Pipet exactly 10 µL of the wormy solution onto a glass slide as a thin streak; do not place the 10 µL as a blob.

steps.title: Count worms on slide
steps.instruction: Under a Leica L2 binocular microscope, follow the streak from left‑to‑right or right‑to‑left and count the worms, using a manual click counter to aid counting.

substeps.instruction: Aim to count between 50 and 150 worms in the 10 µL streak.
If more than 150 worms are observed, dilute the wormy solution and repeat the streak preparation until the count falls within 50–150 worms per 10 µL.
If fewer than 50 worms are observed, increase the volume counted (e.g., use a larger aliquot) to reach the target range.

steps.title: Replicate counts and calculate mean
steps.instruction: Prepare and count two additional slides using the same procedure, then compute the arithmetic mean of the three replicate counts.

substeps.instruction: Use the mean to infer the worm concentration for any desired volume.
The three replicate concentrations provide an estimate of the range within which the true worm concentration lies.
